subject: Exhibit fusion & price consolidation — MSA/order form review
messages:
From: Sara Mills <sara.mills@apexlytics.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@apexlytics.com
Date: 2026-10-28T16:12:00Z
Subject: Request: combine Exhibit C+D into single Exhibit & align order form fees

Jonas —

Thanks again for the demo today. Procurement asked us to propose a narrow change to the MSA/order form so we can simplify internal budget approvals. High level ask: merge Exhibit C (Throughput Schedule) and Exhibit D (Implementation Appendix) into a single Exhibit were calling an "Implementation Appendix" and harmonize the per-token fee bands across both SKUs. The goal is a single sign-off package rather than two parallel exhibits.

Attached is a redline mock that our procurement and finance teams sketched (Apex_Requested_Exhibit_Rebalance_20261028.pdf). Key points:
- Move the ramp milestones into the impl appendix and convert the throughput tiers to a single blended rate table.
- Request a 60-day implementation credit if onboarding extends past Milestone 2.
- Ask that bill run cadence be monthly in arrears rather than net-30 invoice terms.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept a single-exhibit approach from a commercial + legal perspective? If not, what friction points should we expect (billing system, order form parser, SSO of exhibit IDs)? Were trying to keep the paperwork to one signature pass for execs.

cc: jonas, added Karthik for legal redline input. Tom (CFO) will want a short note summarizing risk and any retro price mechanics.

Thanks —
Sara
Sara Mills
Head of Procurement, Apexlytics

Attachment: Apex_Requested_Exhibit_Rebalance_20261028.pdf

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Mills <sara.mills@apexlytics.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-28T18:04:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: combine Exhibit C+D into single Exhibit & align order form fees

Sara —

Appreciate the clear ask and the mock redline. Ive attached our current draft order form with inline comments where the platform/ops team will need a decision (Redwood_Draft_Orderform_20261028.docx). Quick take: conceptually feasible, but a few practical items to flag now so we can give Tom an accurate picture:

1) Billing system: our billing engine treats exhibit IDs as separate charge buckets today. Merging exhibits is doable but requires a mapping step so historical usage aligns to the new blended tiers for the billing run. Thats ultimately a one-time migration but takes ops time.
2) SLA/rollout milestones: combining milestones is fine; well want to preserve Acceptance and Rollback triggers in the merged exhibit.
3) Implementation credit: we can offer a milestone-based credit (applied as offset to first two invoices) — we prefer a clear cap and expiry (e.g., credit applied only if Milestone 2 misses target by >15 days).
4) Net terms: switching to monthly arrears is acceptable but well need to confirm internal finance can process net-0 for the commit component and net-30 for variable usage.

Karthik — can you weigh in on whether legal is comfortable with combining exhibits here, and what redline language youd want for the credit trigger and the blended-rate rollback? Laura — can you confirm how long ops would need to implement the billing mapping if we sign a single-exhibit doc next week?

Next steps proposal: Ill get our legal ops to do a clean tracked-change draft in parallel; Karthik can then do a 1-page memo for Tom summarizing residual legal risk and any audit/retention implications. If all looks ok well route for exec signature by e-sign on DocuSign.

ETA: I can turn the tracked change draft by EOD tomorrow if that works for you.

Cheers,
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, Sara Mills <sara.mills@apexlytics.com>
Date: 2026-10-28T19:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: combine Exhibit C+D into single Exhibit & align order form fees

Jonas / Sara —

Thanks for the context. Quick legal read: merging the exhibits is acceptable from a contract-structure perspective, but we should be explicit about three items in any redline:

• Charge reconciliation: When you convert two rate tables to a blended one, include a reconciliation clause stating how prior invoices are treated (no retroactive refunds unless explicitly agreed). If Apex wants retroactive repricing, well need to scope a transition credit separately.

• Audit & retention: Combined exhibits must still preserve independent acceptance criteria tied to implementation deliverables. Keep Acceptance Tests as a discrete subsection with a cross-reference to the main MSA so the audit trail remains.

• Implementation credit mechanics: Draft language I prefer: "If Milestone 2 completion occurs later than the date specified by >15 calendar days, Redwood will credit Apexlytics an amount equal to X% of the months committed fee for the first billing cycle following Acceptance, capped at Y dollars; credit expires if not applied within 90 days." (We can plug X/Y based on commercial direction.)

I will prepare a tracked-change MSA + single-exhibit order form and include two comment blocks for ops: one explaining the billing bucket migration and one flagging the need for an internal memo for transaction accounting. Ill send the draft to the thread and to Tom for transparency.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachment: (will attach redline draft in next email: Redwood_MSA_Exhibit_Fusion_20261028.docx)

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Mills <sara.mills@apexlytics.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, Tom Li <tom.li@apexlytics.com>
Date: 2026-10-29T21:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: combine Exhibit C+D into single Exhibit & align order form fees

Sara / Tom —

Karthik and Laura have greenlit a path forward. Karthik is producing a tracked-change MSA + consolidated exhibit this evening; Laura confirmed ops estimates ~6 business days to implement the billing mapping once the executed order form lands in our system. The implementation credit language above is our proposed starter point — commercial can adjust X/Y but legal wants the >15-day trigger and 90-day credit expiry retained.

Tom, for a quick CFO summary: merging exhibits reduces Apex internal paperwork by one signature pass but adds an ops-runbook step for Redwood (estimated one-week mapping work). There is no planned retroactive repricing in the proposed redline unless Apex specifically requests a transition credit; any such request would be documented and capped. Net change to Redwood cashflow: minimal timing offset (one-week ops window) — we can provide a short one-page note with the exact ARR impact if youd like.

Sara — if that all sounds ok Ill upload Karthiks redline to the HubSpot deal record and initiate the DocuSign envelope pending your confirmation.

Thanks,
Jonas
